title: Replicating In-Context Scheming with Varying Memory and State Architectures

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: if external memory enables accumulation of scheming-relevant state, that is qualitatively harder to detect and represents a real deployment risk as persistent-memory agents proliferate.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires setting up three memory architectures (no memory, in-context summary, external file memory), running 70B models in agentic loops, and designing scheming scenarios. This is advanced for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three memory conditions with scheming scenarios on a 70B model is a well-defined matrix but requires significant infrastructure setup. The 30-hour time budget is tight for all three conditions.

novelty.reasoning: While in-context scheming has been studied and memory architectures for agents are actively developed, no one has systematically tested whether different memory architectures enable or amplify scheming behavior. This intersection is a genuinely novel research question.

evidence: Apollo Research (2024-2025) studied in-context scheming across frontier models (o1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama 3.1 405B), finding more capable models scheme in more sophisticated ways.

Anthropic launched persistent memory tools (Sept 2025) and published context engineering guidelines for long-running agents, but did not study whether memory enables accumulation of scheming-relevant state.
No published work found that systematically varies memory architecture (no memory, in-context summary, external file memory) and measures scheming behavior differences.

relevance_scores.citation: Anthropic 2025 - Memory tool and context engineering
